Welcome to Mereworth
We are a thriving and popular one form entry village school, situated midway between Maidstone and Tonbridge with close proximity to Kings Hill.
Everyone who works at Mereworth Community Primary School is completely committed to giving the children the very best learning opportunities to ensure that they have every opportunity to succeed in the future. This is supported by our Values Based Education, and this September our value is Positivity.
"As parents, we instantly got a warm, nurturing feeling from the school."

Musical Opportunities
Music Lessons – As of September 2026, the following lessons are available at Mereworth Community School:
Voice, Signing & Drama Tuition
Rocksteady Music School
Music plays a very important role at Mereworth Community Primary School and we are proud of all the concerts and performances we give throughout the year.
We are proud to be a singing school and have achieved the Gold Sing-Up Award. We have weekly singing assemblies and a thriving KS2 choir that takes part in annual local and national events including ‘Young Voices’ at the 02 in London and the Hillview/Tonbridge Arts Festival.
Our Year 3 children receive 30 weeks of recorder tuition funded by the government’s ‘music plus’ scheme, which is continued when they get to Year 6.

We had a fantastic time taking part and we are incredibly proud of all the children who represented the school with such enthusiasm, confidence and talent.
Our KS2 choir achieved wonderful success, bringing home two awards:
· 1st Place – Lower KS2 (Years 3 & 4) Musical Theatre Song with "This Is Me"
· 3rd Place – Upper KS2 (Years 5 & 6) Pop Song with "Riptide"
Alongside their award-winning performances, our Lower KS2 choir also performed the pop song "Diamonds", while our Upper KS2 choir delighted the audience with the musical theatre favourite "Never Enough".
We were also thrilled with the results of the festival's Art Competition, themed "Under the Sea". You can see the entries here. Congratulations to our prize winners:
A huge well done to every child who took part. Their hard work, creativity and dedication made us all incredibly proud. Congratulations to everyone involved for another successful year at the Tonbridge Primary Arts Festival!

We had a fantastic time at Young Voices 2026, and the children who took part were amazing ambassadors for our school. They had a wonderful experience and participated in the Young Voices Worldwide Wicked Singalong live stream, which they also thoroughly enjoyed.

The concerts included performances from the choir, KS1 singing club, guitarists, drummers, voice, piano, woodwind and strings.Year 3 also performed 3 songs on the recorder, which they have been learning since September as part of the Music Plus sessions. Well done to all the children you were all amazing.

Visitors & Trips
At Mereworth Community Primary School, we believe that learning is enriched when children have opportunities to experience the wider world. Throughout the academic year, pupils in every year group take part in a variety of educational visits and welcome a range of visitors into school to enhance and extend their learning.
We regularly invite visitors into school to bring learning to life and provide children with hands-on experiences linked to the curriculum.
These opportunities have previously included:
Year 6 pupils also benefit from a range of workshops designed to support their transition to secondary school. These include visits from magistrates and police officers, money management workshops and the ‘Safety in Action’ programme, which helps children develop the knowledge and confidence to respond safely and responsibly to new scenarios.
Educational visits provide valuable opportunities for children to deepen their understanding of topics studied in class and to develop their independence, confidence and curiosity.
Trips are carefully planned to support the curriculum and may include visits to local and national places of interest, such as:
Children in the KS2 Choir also have the opportunity to perform at special events including the Young Voices concert at the O2 Arena and the Hillfest Music Festival in Tonbridge.
Year 5 and Year 6 pupils also take part in residential visits during the summer term which provides further opportunities for the children to develop teamwork, resilience and independence while creating lasting memories with their classmates.

pageCache.text:
Sensory Garden
Our beautiful sensory garden was designed and created by our site manager Mr Hyder in 2023 - transforming an unused area of brambles and scrub into a calm, reflective and uplifting space for the whole school community.
Since its 'grand opening' to children and parents, which included tours hosted by our Year 6 children, the garden has continued to grow - with plants maturing and self seeding and new features being added. The final addition will be a water feature built from a series of salvaged Belfast sinks. This gentle waterfall will provide drinking and washing water for wildlife and attract creatures such as dragonflies and damselflies, whilst the burbling of the water will enhance the existing soundscape.
Summer in the garden - 2026
Our intentions for the garden:
A welcoming environment for wildlife
Garden facts:
Wind chimes and metal garden art
Learning and seating areas

flower garden

With huge thanks to:
Feedback from some of our visitors:
“I think what you have all achieved with the sensory garden and pond area is fantastic. I could see how much effort had gone into making all these areas relaxing, environmentally friendly, and educational. It was all superb and I hope that the children appreciate and enjoy this space as much as I did. Mr Hyder and the other volunteers have done such an exceptional job and they should all be very proud of themselves.”
“The year 6’s should be so proud of themselves for the tours and how they conducted themselves. The sensory garden is looking amazing and I can’t wait to see it again once it is more established, the children are so lucky!”

Mathematics Overview
At Mereworth, we believe that Mathematics is a key skill and has an important part to play in our daily lives. It underpins many other areas of the Curriculum such as Geography, History, Science, Art, Design and Technology. Consequently, it is essential that Mathematics teaching and learning is engaging, meaningful to the World in which we live, and accessible to all of the children in School helping to engender a sense of enjoyment and curiosity about Mathematics.
We aim to develop independent learners that are able and confident to apply their Mathematic skills to a variety of scenarios to enable them to have a range of strategies and approaches to solving problems. All children need a deep understanding of the Mathematics they are learning, key measures of this are their ability to solve increasingly complex problems, doing so with fluency.
Mathematics National Curriculum
At Mereworth we have adopted a ‘mastery’ approach to the teaching, learning and assessment of Mathematics, underpinned by our Assessment system ; 21 Steps (please see link on our website). This ensures that children are able to master the curriculum and gain a thorough understanding of all topics covered.
At Mereworth we use the “Maths No Problem” programme of study and NCETM (‘National Centre of Excellence of Teaching Mathematics’) materials and resources to support the teaching of Mathematics in each year group.

Emile Education Tournaments
The Emile range of resources had been developed by a group of teachers, academics and game developers. Together they developed and supply games-based learning resources to over 15% of the primary schools in the UK & Ireland. Their range of resources are all underpinned by robust pedagogical research and are tested rigorously by teachers in real classrooms.
Our children at Mereworth began competing in Emile Tournaments September 2022. Throughout our first academic year the number of children getting involved increased from one class to the whole school. Their number facts knowledge and times tables confidence progressed immensely, whilst the tournaments gave them a reason to practise and improve. The MTC tournaments resemble the same conditions of the Year 4 Multiplication Check, so is a great opportunity for them to practise their skills and speed.
Firstly, the children compete in the Regional Tournament against local schools. If they are successful enough on this leaderboard, usually second or first place, the children are placed into the National Finals the following week. The children have time in school on computers and have access to the school ipads to enhance their scores over the two days of competition, but can also access the platform at home.
Due to the amazing impact these tournaments have, they are getting more popular each year. There are thousands more children competing each tournament across the country. Mereworth children getting into the National Finals is an incredible achievement and we are incredibly proud of them.
The children’s enthusiasm and competitiveness steer the tournaments and this has greatly improved the fluency and automaticity of their times table and number knowledge. The children love the competitive element of the tournament and really try hard to rise to the challenge.

Music Overview
Music is an integral part of life at Mereworth Community Primary School and is taught in every year group.
Weekly singing assemblies are held using the digital resource Sing Up. We are very proud to be holders of the Gold Sing Up Award, recognising our strong commitment to singing across the school. At Mereworth, there is a thriving Key Stage 1 Singing Club and a Key Stage 2 Choir, both of which perform at concerts and events throughout the school year.
As part of their music education, children take part in singing, listening to and appraising music, playing instruments and composing. We use a variety of resources, including Sing Up and Charanga, an interactive digital music scheme. In Year 3, children receive 30 weeks of recorder tuition as part of the Government’s “Music Plus” scheme. Across all other year groups, pupils experience playing a range of tuned and untuned instruments during their music lessons.
Throughout the year, children are given many opportunities to perform, including assemblies, the Christmas Nativity and Carol Concert, Rocksteady Concert, Voice Tuition Concert, the Spring Music Concert, the Tonbridge Arts Festival, Young Voices and Mereworth’s Got Talent!

Our Governors
Welcome to our Governors page. To find out more about our Governing Body, please choose from the links below. If you wish to contact the Governing Body, please do so via email to amorris@mereworth.kent.sch.uk for the attention of the Clerk, Adam Blakemore.
Pamela Conibeer - Chair of Governors
My name is Pamela Conibeer and my husband and I have been residents of Mereworth for almost twenty years, having moved here from Essex early in 1991. My own background is in education, as we moved to Kent in order for me to take up a previous post as Headteacher of a girls secondary school in Medway.
I became a Community Governor in 2009 during a period of change and development for the school, which has always been at the heart of the village community, and I feel it is both a pleasure and a privilege to be part of the team as the school goes from strength to strength.
I am also the Chair of the Management Committee of The Rowans which is a Pupil Referral Unit in Walderslade, Medway.
Liz Windon - Vice Chair of Governors, Chair of Teaching & Learning, SEND Governor
I have worked in the Education sector for the last 31 years
I now specialise in providing independent consultancy support to schools to set up effective pupil tracking systems and assist them in the analysis of internal and external data as evidence to support their own school evaluation
I have been involved, as a LA officer, independent data consultant and a school governor, in providing evidence for Ofsted inspections which have proved effective in improving judgement on standards of achievement and progress.
I have been a school governor for the last 26 years in a number of Primary schools in Medway and Kent, and now in my 7th year at Mereworth. I am currently also a governor at Victoria Road Primary School in Ashford.
Esther Jenner - Chair of Finance & Resources / Health & Safety Governor
I have lived in Mereworth since 2013 with my family. I have 2 children who will both be attending Mereworth Primary School by September 2022.
I am currently a bookkeeper and received my AAT qualification in 2019. My job involves working for several different size companies looking at their finances and helping them with financial decisions to aid their businesses.
Prior to be being a bookkeeper, I worked as an estate agent running a small business and taking control of day to day running and the finances. I helped start the business from the beginning and built it up to what is now a successful estate agency.
A few years back I realised there was a need for communication within the Mereworth community, so I set up the Mereworth Group Facebook page which is ongoing.
Amanda Lavelle - Headteacher
I have worked in education for 30 years across two local authorities and a range of primary schools of varying sizes. Throughout my career, I have developed extensive experience in school leadership, strategic development and governance. I have previously served as both a staff governor and a headteacher governor and now serve as headteacher on the governing body of Mereworth Community Primary School. I am committed to ensuring high standards of education, strong accountability and continuous school improvement.
Kate Maryon - Staff Governor
I am the Y6 teacher and Deputy Headteacher at Mereworth and have also been staff governor on the Governing Body for the last 17 years. During this time I have mostly supported the teaching and learning committee.
I have been in education for 30 years, teaching in 4 schools in this time in the Maidstone and Edenbridge area. In my previous post as DHT of Coxheath school, I also formed part of the governing body.
Simon Phillips - EYFS & OPAL Governor
Both my children have been at Mereworth school for 3 years, having moved from a 2 form entry school in Bromley. When looking for schools we were instantly struck by the warm, welcoming and personal feeling present at Mereworth, which set it apart from the others we looked at.
I have worked in the defence sector for 18 years, with experience in strategic and management roles as well as H&S and training.
Through these roles I have become very familiar with the ever-evolving challenge that digital and online security present to our young people, and indeed to us as parents and guardians trying to keep them safe. I am keen to use my knowledge to enrich our understanding and approach to this relatively new and complex challenge.
Nesceita Brooks
My name is Nessie Brooks.
I have lived in Mereworth for more than 14 years now, with Mereworth School practically on my doorstep.
My work as an Occupational Health professional has seen me working extensively with Kent and London schools for more than 35 years providing support and advice regarding health and wellbeing to ALL staff. I understand the budgetary constraints schools are currently faced with to deliver an education to our children in this ever changing world (and government).
I started working independently at the start of the Covid pandemic concentrating on advising headteachers and school staff to inform their decision making. I also provided first contact counselling by listening to their anxieties about having to continue going into the workplace, and / or providing online teaching.
I also have a great deal of experience working with all of the other sectors too.
I am excited to be a Governor for Mereworth School.
Kim Winterbottom - Safeguarding Governor & Climate Change and Sustainability
My name is Kim Winterbottom and I’m the SENCO, union rep and a year 3 teacher at another local school which works collaboratively with Mereworth. I have a degree in childhood studies with special educational needs, PGCE and a masters degree in psychology which has given me a good understanding of many aspects of learning and wellbeing. I recognise the importance of inclusion and children feeling safe, happy and connected within school.
I’m passionate about the environment and politics so I’m also involved in Tonbridge and Malling Green party where I volunteer as the candidate agent. I stood as a candidate in local elections for Mereworth and as a candidate in the last parliamentary election for a neighbouring constituency. I’m particularly interested in social justice within the community so enjoy learning more about local governance and the impact this has on people’s lives in our community.
It has been a privilege getting to know the wonderful children and fantastic staff in this truly lovely school.
Nicola Wilcher - Wellbeing Governor
My name is Nicola Wilcher and I live in Kings Hill with my husband. I work as a Teaching Assistant at Kings Hill school and have done so for the past two years. My career has predominantly been working as a nanny for a variety of families looking after new-borns through to teenagers. What I love about working with children is that no day is ever the same. We can also learn from children as they often bring new knowledge in to the classroom during lessons. I understand the importance of a good education and the need for the right resources to enable this to happen. I am very pleased to be joining the board of governors and to be making a positive contribution in improving the school’s standing in the community.
Lis Clarke - Pupil Premium Governor
My name is Lis Clarke, and I have worked in leadership and strategic operational roles for over 15 years, with a focus on growing businesses and driving efficiencies. My previous experience includes serving as Operations Director at FENSA, the leading window and door installation competent person scheme, which is authorised by government (MHCLG) and accredited by the United Kingdom Accreditation Service. I have also worked with other certification and membership bodies in highly regulated environments.
I have particular expertise in strategic operations and compliance, and I hold an Economics degree from the University of Surrey.
I share my life with my partner, our two daughters, and our two family dogs. I have lived in and around Maidstone for over 20 years and am proud to have two nephews attending Mereworth School.
As a school governor, I value the opportunity to contribute my experience and support the school’s continued growth and success.
Aaron Day - Parent Governor
I am delighted to have joined the governing body as a Parent Governor. I have two daughters with a connection to the Mereworth School— my youngest is currently a pupil here, and my eldest recently completed her time at the school having joined after a period of home education. The warmth, care, and dedication shown by the staff in helping her settle into Mereworth life made a profound difference to our family, and it is an experience that has given me enormous respect and admiration for everything the school stands for. Professionally, I work as a Simulation Engineer in the aerospace industry. I am a strong advocate for the importance of STEM subjects from an early age, and I am passionate about helping children appreciate just how broad and varied the career paths are that draw on science, technology, engineering, and mathematics — from medicine and architecture to software, aviation, and beyond. As a governor, my aim is simply to support the school in any way I can. Whether that means contributing my professional perspective, engaging with the wider school community, or rolling up my sleeves for whatever is needed, I am committed to playing my part in helping every child here thrive. I very much look forward to working with the staff, fellow governors, and families to support the continued success of the school.
Dawn Vidgen
My name is Dawn Vidgen and I am delighted to have joined the Governing Body at Merworth Community school. I currently work at another local primary school as the EYFS Lead and have worked in education for the past 10 years.
Throughout my career, I have been passionate about supporting children in the early stages of their education and ensuring they have the very best start to school life. I have a particular interest in early reading, child development and creating nurturing environments where children feel happy, safe and inspired to learn.
I am looking forward to supporting the school community and working alongside staff, governors and families to help the school continue to flourish.
Jamie Weare
I have worked as a Secondary School History teacher for 11 years, with over 9 years’ experience as a pastoral leader. This has given me valuable insight into the importance of early years and primary education in shaping a child’s academic journey. It has also provided me with a strong understanding of the demands placed on school staff, as well as the processes involved in developing and consistently implementing whole-school policies.
Since relocating from London three years ago, Mereworth has become home for me and my family. With my daughter due to start at Mereworth this September, I am keen to play my part in ensuring the school continues to go from strength to strength.
Darren Palmer
Having lived in the area for around 25 years, I look forward to being a member of Mereworth Primary School’s Governing Body.
I have worked in secondary education for just under 30 years with around 20 of those at senior leadership level in South London. The roles have been varied with pastoral, curriculum and oversight threads, allowing me to have understanding of the challenges faced by each area of school life.
Through my previous Trust there have been many opportunities where I had the chance to work directly with primary colleagues and primary pupils. This included working as a Governor for one of the Trust’s Primary School. It’s clear there’s a vast amount of skills and strategies that one sector can learn from the other.
Since 1990 I have been a Scout Leader working across age groups but mainly with Cub Scouts aged eight to ten and a half. For Mereworth & Kings Hill, the section is based at Mereworth School. It is clear that children who attend the school are rightly proud.
Supporting Mereworth School as a Governor is a way I am able to help share my knowledge and skills with a team of likeminded people. There’s no doubt ensuring pupils are looked after and are happy in their school means each child can achieve.
Governors Arrangements
The Governing Body of Mereworth Primary School is made up of 13 Governors. There are: 2 Staff Governors (including the Headteacher), 2 Parent Governors, 1 Local Authority Governor and 8 Co-opted Governors.
Co-opted Governors are appointed by the Governing Body and are people who have the skills required to contribute to the effective governance and success of the school. All our governors bring a rich and varied range of experience and expertise from their working backgrounds.
The full Governing Body meets three times per year and, in addition, we have committees to consider the different aspects of the school in more detail.
These committees are:
1 The Finance and Resources CommitteeThis committee focuses on health and safety, finance, premises, personnel matters and oversees the use and outcomes of specifically directed funding for identified pupil groups.
2 The Teaching and Learning CommitteeThis committee focuses on our curriculum provision, the outcomes of all pupils including pupils with SEND, the allocation of specific grants and their impact on pupil progress and attainment.
3 The Pay and Performance CommitteeThe committee meets on 2 occasions per year to oversee the arrangements and outcomes of the Pay and Performance procedures for the teaching staff and the support staff to ensure that these are fair and equitable and in accordance with required processes. This committee also oversees the annual appraisal process for the Headteacher in liaison with the external advisor.
All governing body meetings take place face to face.

SEND
Special Educational Needs and Disability Information
Special Educational Needs Co-ordinator (SENCO): Mrs Kathryn Delaney
Designated Teacher for Children in Care (DLAC) : Mrs Kathryn Delaney
Our SENCO/DLAC can be contacted via the school office: 01622 812569
Email: senco@mereworth.kent.sch.uk
At Mereworth Community Primary School, we have high expectations for all the children that we teach regardless of their educational need. All children with SEND are treated as individuals and our staff and curriculum supports and enhances the learning of all the children in our care.
We are proud to be an inclusive school with our children being at the centre of all the decisions about their learning. We aim to prepare our children for each stage of their learning and transition between year groups and Key Stages, as well as onwards into the future. We are committed to making the appropriate provision for all our pupils and ensure inclusion. All our pupils have a right to full and equal access to the curriculum to enable them to reach their full potential.
It is the SENCO’s responsibility to ensure that provision is effective for all vulnerable children with SEND, have English as and Additional Language (EAL) and are Looked After Children (or previously Looked After Children) LAC.
Our percentage of children with SEND is above national average.

Supporting Children with SEND
At Mereworth Community Primary School we want all of our children to be challenged to meet their full potential. All our teachers are well trained in supporting the needs of children with SEND. This training is regularly updated. Working closely together as a team, we ensure there is early identification of any needs and work closely with parents, children and professionals. We believe that this strong working relationship with parents and children is critical to all support given.
Children who have been identified as having additional support are included in the Class Provision Map. This identifies all the in-class support and interventions that are accessed by each child. Those children who have an EHCP or who are on a pathway for an EHCP have their own Personalised Provision Maps tailored to their needs and EHCP recommendations for support.
Our teaching staff have high expectations of all of the children in our care. Meetings are held termly to discuss children across the school in receipt of support, to identify those who require additional support. Personal targets are set that are achievable yet challenging and these are regularly reviewed in our Pupil Progress Meetings and through the ‘Graduated Approach’.
Interventions are run across the school by qualified members of staff, to complement the quality first teaching from the classroom. Interventions are ‘live’ and delivered daily to address any misconceptions, this then enables the children to continue to access the learning. Specific targets are timetabled on a weekly basis e.g. Lego Therapy.
Quality First Teaching
All of our pupils have access to ‘High Quality First Teaching’ is essential for all children being able to achieve their best outcomes, especially those who are vulnerable and disadvantaged.
Teachers ensure that lessons are designed to meet the needs of all learners by using a range of tools – adaptive teaching, scaffolding and modelling, active engagement, formative assessment and a highly structured environment that allows for excellent communication with minimal distraction.
Examples of Quality First Teaching seen in the classroom are: use of visual aids, peer support, chunking of instructions, small group working, word banks/mats and high-quality questioning.
Class Teachers, the Headteacher and SENCO meet on a termly basis to discuss attainment and progress of all children, as well as well-being and barriers to learning. Interventions are planned around the needs of the classes and the school with teaching assistants being deployed appropriately. Children can also be allocated time with the school- based counsellor.
Mainstream Core Standards
The Mainstream Core Standards (MCS) are developed by the Local Authority and detail what constitutes as best practice for all children not just those with SEND.
All teaching staff have received training on the MCS and use the information to support and identify children who require additional support and/or interventions.Mainstream Core Standards

Primary Science Overview
At Mereworth Community Primary, we believe science helps children make sense of the world around them. Through carefully planned lessons, children learn to ask questions, make predictions, and explore ideas using simple, practical investigations. We encourage curiosity and support pupils to build secure scientific knowledge step by step, in line with the expectations of the National Curriculum for England.
Our approach places a strong emphasis on scientific skills as well as scientific facts. Children learn how to observe closely, measure accurately, record findings, and explain what they have discovered. They also develop understanding of key topics such as plants, animals including humans, materials, forces, and Earth and space, using age-appropriate resources and real-life examples where possible.
We welcome parents to support learning at home by noticing science in everyday life—such as discussing how plants grow, talking about weather and seasons, or exploring changes in materials during cooking and cleaning. If you would like more information about what your child is learning, or suggestions for simple science activities, please speak to your child’s class teacher. Together, we can help children build confidence and a lifelong interest in science.
We follow the Kent Primary Science Scheme of work 2024, which has 28 units of study. Each unit of study has been assigned to a particular year group in line with guidance from the New National Curriculum 2024.

House and Sports Captains
At Mereworth Community Primary School, all Year 6 pupils are encouraged to take on leadership and responsibility roles across the school. Children apply for positions such as House and Sports Captains by explaining why they would be strong candidates before pupils vote democratically for their representatives. Successful candidates act as positive role models, support whole-school events such as Sports Day and proudly lead tours during open days. Sports Captains also take on additional responsibilities throughout the year, including organising events such as the Mini Wimbledon tournaments in the summer, helping to coordinate visits from professional athletes and managing the ordering of new sports equipment using the funds raised from these events. In addition, they are responsible for setting out scooters and ezy riders for pupils to use during playtimes and lunchtimes. It is always wonderful to see the children beam with pride as they speak so enthusiastically about our school community. These opportunities help to develop teamwork, communication and leadership skills, while promoting the values of responsibility and active citizenship that are central to school life.

Curriculum Overview
Mereworth Community Primary School curriculum vision
Mereworth Community Primary School’s curriculum will provide our children with ‘Lasting Learning Experiences for Life’. At Mereworth we offer a rich and vibrant curriculum which is ambitious for all learners and aims to produce confident and self-motivated pupils who are eager to learn. Our curriculum helps children develop the essential knowledge, skills and understanding they need to equip themselves for ‘Lifelong Learning’ and the 21st century world. It encompasses the formal requirements of the National Curriculum, and is enhanced by our 5 Core School Values, taking our pupils’ education beyond the experiences of the classroom, to ensure that they are exposed to the richest and most varied learning opportunities.
